H8NY06048.name: Gregory Meeks
H8NY06048.bio: Senior member of the House Financial Services Committee who grew up in public housing.

positions.stance: Wants to expand access to capital, credit and wealth-building tools, especially for historically underserved communities, and to hold Wall Street accountable.
Supports universal background checks, banning assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, closing loopholes, and community violence intervention programs.
"Access to healthcare is a human right"; supports protecting the Affordable Care Act, Medicare and Medicaid, and investing in mental health and maternal care.
Supports comprehensive reform with a path to citizenship for Dreamers, TPS holders, farmworkers and essential workers, while securing borders and holding serious offenders accountable.
"All workers deserve the right to unionize and collectively bargain."

H8PA07200.name: Mary Gay Scanlon
H8PA07200.bio: Vice Chair of the House Judiciary Committee and longtime education rights advocate.

positions.stance: Has cosponsored legislation to close loopholes, improve background checks, and ban assault rifles.
Supports expanding early childhood education, fairly funding schools, and fully funding IDEA and Title I.
Calls climate change a serious threat; supports reducing carbon emissions and protecting the Clean Air and Clean Water Acts.
Supports reducing the influence of money in politics, protecting and expanding voting rights, and restoring ethics to government.
Supports safeguarding the Affordable Care Act, lowering prescription drug costs, and protecting reproductive rights.

H8PA13125.name: John Joyce
H8PA13125.bio: Physician who practiced medicine in Pennsylvania for over 25 years before joining Congress.

positions.stance: Working to defend constitutional rights, rebuild the economy, improve health care, strengthen national security, and support farmers and agriculture.
Supports a pro-growth agenda and bringing family-sustaining jobs home to Pennsylvania for American workers.
Working to roll back burdensome regulations, lower energy costs for families, and create energy jobs in the region.
Focused on protecting Medicare, investing in medical innovation, combating the drug crisis, and growing the local doctor pipeline.
Says the U.S. must keep rebuilding its military and counter the growing threat of the Chinese Communist Party.

H2PA17103.name: Chris Deluzio
H2PA17103.bio: Navy veteran and voting rights attorney (from his 2022 survey).

positions.stance: Believes in "a government that serves all of us -- not just the biggest and most powerful corporations."
Wants more manufacturing done in western Pennsylvania by union workers and opposes shipping jobs overseas.
Calls for bold action to protect democracy from limitless corporate money, voter suppression and gerrymandering.
Supports the PRO Act and making it easier for workers to form and join a union.
Wants trade policies that let farmers compete, calling it unfair that U.S. farm exports face high tariffs abroad.
Says federal spending is "out of control" and seeks to instill fiscal discipline in government.
Supports investing in cutting-edge technologies to preserve military superiority and deter rogue states.
Says education policy works best at the state and local level; supports giving parents freedom to guide their children's education.
Supports increasing domestic oil and gas supply while exploring alternative energy sources and stewarding natural resources.
Supports an America First policy, opposing endless foreign wars and job offshoring, and calls securing the border "non-negotiable."
Committed to lowering taxes, cutting regulations, rebuilding manufacturing, and protecting American industries from unfair foreign trade practices.
Supports expanding domestic energy development, including oil, natural gas and clean coal, to cut reliance on foreign energy.
Fighting for health care price transparency, lower drug prices, and cutting wasteful spending in the health system.
Committed to expanding veterans' health care options, streamlining benefits, and ensuring timely, high-quality care.

H4OH09169.name: Derek Merrin
H4OH09169.bio: Former Ohio state representative (from his 2024 survey).

positions.stance: Supports a constitutional amendment requiring a balanced budget.
Supports sending the military to secure the border, finishing the border wall, and deporting illegal immigrants.
Will protect earned benefits and supports removing the federal tax on Social Security benefits.
Says he led efforts in Ohio to cut the state income tax, reduce regulations, and expand school choice.
Supports a constitutional amendment imposing term limits on Members of Congress.

H2OH14064.name: David Joyce
H2OH14064.bio: Former Geauga County Prosecutor and member of the House Appropriations Committee.

positions.stance: Wants bipartisan solutions to increase border security, combat drug trafficking, and fix the "broken immigration system."
Supports funding military readiness, supporting troops at home and abroad, and caring for military families.
Calls himself "a staunch supporter of our first responders and law enforcement officers."
Will keep working across the aisle to secure investments to restore and protect the Great Lakes.
Supports fiscally responsible policies, cutting red tape, creating good-paying jobs, and jobs-training programs.

H2GA12121.name: Rick Allen
H2GA12121.bio: Small business owner for almost 40 years and member of the House Agriculture Committee.

positions.stance: Committed to a strong farm bill and ensuring the safest, most abundant and most affordable food supply in the world.
Promotes conservative economic policies that create jobs and reduce the size and scope of the federal government.
Wants K-12 education to remain local with appropriate federal support; a vocal supporter of school choice.
Supports a small federal government, less regulation and lower taxes, with responsibility returned to the states.
Wants to disband the U.S. Department of Education and return education to state and local authorities.
Wants to "Protect Innocent Human Life, from Conception until Natural Death" and opposes abortion.
Opposes gender-transition medical procedures for minors.

H6NC11321.name: Jennifer Balkcom
H6NC11321.bio: North Carolina state representative who grew up on a family farm in Henderson County.

positions.stance: Highlights her state laws strengthening penalties for violent offenders and protections against exploitation of women and minors.
Supports disaster relief for farmers and protecting U.S. farmland from foreign ownership.
Wants to secure infrastructure and other critical funding for Henderson County.
Passionate about "ensuring fairness and equal opportunity for women and girls in athletic competition."

H4MI07103.name: Tim Walberg
H4MI07103.bio: Former pastor; chairman of the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

positions.stance: Supports protecting farmland from purchase by foreign adversaries and opposes excessive regulations on farmers.
Says he looks for opportunities to move good ideas forward by working with colleagues on both sides of the aisle.
Committed to keeping America safe and giving troops the best training, equipment and resources.
Supports returning education control to parents and local communities, school choice, and simplifying federal student aid.
Calls for an "all-of-the-above" America first energy strategy to achieve energy independence and lower utility bills.
Supports federal funding for beach replenishment, clean water initiatives, and preventing offshore drilling off the New Jersey coast.
Says "a public servant's greatest responsibility is to protect those who cannot defend themselves," including combating human trafficking.
Believes veterans' needs "must come first in the queue for federal funding."
